Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA comer Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http://www.dilg.com.ph 23 AUG 2019 CILG OPINION NO. -40-- CARLO JAMES B. LOSORATA SK Chairman Barangay Cansuje Argao, Cebu Dear SK Chairman Losorata: s. 202 This has reference to your letter dated 29 January 2019 requesting for legal opinion relative to the taxing power of barangay. In your letter, the queries are as follows: 1. 2. 3. Can we tax those hog raisers/poultry farmers that sell their product not to marginal farmers or fishermen? How much tax can we impose? Can we tax, say, fifty (Php 50.00) per hog being sold? Can we impose taxes on computer shops? Can we impose tax on the newly opened resort that charge admission fees and is within the territorial jurisdiction of the barangay? We find Section 152 of Republic Act No. 7160, otherwise known as the Local Government Code of 1991, applicable. It provides for the scope of the taxing powers of the barangay. It states: Section 152. Scope of Taxing Powers. - The barangays may levy taxes, fees, and charges, as provided in this Article, which shall exclusively accrue to them: (a) Taxes - On stores or retailers with fixed business establishments with gross sales of receipts of the preceding calendar year of Fifty thousand pesos (P50, 000.00) or less, in the case of cities and Thirty thousand pesos (P30,000.OO) or less, in the case of municipalities, at a rate not exceeding one percent (1%) on such gross sales or receipts. (b) Service Fees or Charges. Barangays may collect reasonable fees or charges for services rendered in connection with the regulations or the use of barangay-owned properties or service facilities such as palay, copra, or tobacco dryers.

(c) xxx (Amended by Republic Act No. 11032, otherwise known as the "Ease of Doing Business and Efficient Government Service Delivery Act of 2018") (d) Other fees and Charges. - The barangay may levy reasonable fees and charges: (I) On commercial breeding of fighting cocks, cockfights and cockpits; (2) On places of recreation which charge admission fees; and (3) On billboards, signboards, neon signs, and outdoor advertisements. Accordingly, the phrase "As provided in this article" limits the power of the barangay to impose taxes, fees and charges only to those enumerated above. Should the object to be taxed is not one of those enumerated in Section 152 of RA 7160, then the barangay has no authority to impose taxes, fees and charges on the same. Further, Section 143(h) of RA 7160 provides that the Municipality/City has the authority to tax on any business that the sanggunian concerned may deem proper to tax. Thus, those that are not taxable by the provinces or the barangays are within the taxing authority of the City or Municipality. On the first and second queries, we opine in the negative. The hog raising/poultry farming and the computer shops are not one of those enumerated above that the barangay may impose tax, fees and charges on. Consequently, barangay has no legal basis to impose tax, fees and charges on the same except for imposition of fees and charges on services rendered as provided in Section 152(b) and Section 153 of RA 7160. 1 Notwithstanding, we previously opined that if, however, there are businesses not yet the subject of any tax by the national, provincial, municipal or city government, then per Section 186 of RA 7160, the barangay can impose a tax on the same. It is understood that the business is conducted within the territorial jurisdiction of the barangay.2 As to the third query, our view is also in the negative. The law does not give the barangay authority to tax on places of recreation which charge admission fees. Our view is that it is correct to include resorts within the purview of "places of recreation." However, the law clearly provides that the barangay may levy fees and charges on places of recreation which charge admission fees. Thus, what the barangay may impose on places of recreation, such as resorts, are fees and charges but not tax. This is in line with our previous opinion in which we state: "In relation to cinemas and other recreation business, it is unfortunate to note that a barangay is not given the power to tax but nonetheless, it is given the power to impose fees and charges per Section 152(d)(2) of the Local Government Code. This opinion is solely based on the facts given in the letter query and is not without prejudice to any contrary opinion of the Department of Finance, which is the government agency with the mandate and ertise to give authoritative opinion on the matter. Very truly yours, he authority of he Secretary A IN B. DINO ndersecretary LLLS/42
